name: Create allocations table with start and end dates and vacate reason
w: An allocation is the join between a resident and a bed over a date range. Modelling it as dated history rather than a status flag on the bed is what makes occupancy reporting, fee proration and dispute handling possible later.
ac: allocations has hostel_id, resident_id, bed_id, room_id, start_date, end_date, status, rent_override and created_by
Foreign keys defined with deliberate delete behaviour that never cascades away history
Indexes support fast lookup of the live allocation for a bed and for a resident
RLS enabled with the hostel-scoped pattern
Only one row per bed can have a null end_date
out: No pricing snapshot per allocation beyond an optional rent override.

name: Implement bed allocation from a vacant bed
w: This is the daily core action in the product. It must be a single atomic step so a bed can never appear occupied without a resident, or occupied by two residents.
ac: A vacant bed can be allocated to an active resident with a start date
The bed status and the allocation row are written in one transaction
A resident who already holds a live bed is blocked with an explicit message
Beds are chosen from a list of actually vacant beds; free-text entry is not possible
The actor, timestamp and hostel are recorded on the allocation
out: No advance booking of a future bed, and no waitlist.

name: Prevent double allocation of the same bed for overlapping dates
w: Two residents holding one bed is the single most damaging data-integrity failure in hostel software: it corrupts occupancy, fees and the owner's trust in the product. This is enforced in the database, not only in the UI.
ac: A database-level constraint rejects overlapping active allocations for one bed
Two simultaneous allocation requests for the same bed result in exactly one row
A historical allocation on the same bed with non-overlapping dates is still allowed
The user sees a clear message naming the conflicting resident and dates
A concurrency integration test proves the behaviour with parallel requests
out: No automatic reallocation or suggestion engine when a conflict occurs.

name: Implement bed vacate and room transfer flow
w: Residents leave and move rooms constantly. A transfer must never leave a resident holding two beds or one bed claimed by two residents, even for a moment.
ac: Vacate closes the allocation with an end date and a reason and frees the bed
Transfer closes the previous allocation and opens the new one in a single transaction
A failure during transfer rolls back both changes completely
The old bed becomes available and the new bed becomes occupied atomically
Outstanding fee implications are surfaced to the user before confirming the transfer
out: No refund or settlement calculation is performed in this task.

name: Calculate occupied and vacant bed counts from allocations
w: Occupancy is the headline number an owner judges the product by, and it is the number most likely to be wrong if it is stored instead of derived. It is therefore always computed from live allocations.
ac: Counts are derived only from live allocations, never from a stored counter
Per-room, per-floor and per-hostel totals are consistent with each other
Vacated and blocked beds are excluded correctly from vacancy
A SQL fixture test asserts the expected counts against seeded data
Performance is acceptable at 500 beds across 100 rooms
out: No historical occupancy snapshots for backdated reporting in the MVP.

name: Build occupancy snapshot view per hostel and floor
w: Owners and wardens need to see, floor by floor, which beds are free, so they can answer enquiries without walking the building.
ac: The view shows floor, then room, then each bed with its live status
Occupancy percentage is shown per floor and for the whole hostel
Allocating or vacating updates the view without a full page reload
A 500 bed hostel renders within an acceptable time
Blocked and maintenance beds are visually distinct from vacant beds
out: No graphical floor plan or drag-and-drop bed assignment.

name: Add allocation history and audit trail
w: Allocation disputes are a routine conversation with residents and parents. Having an immutable record of who moved where, when and who recorded it settles the argument in seconds.
ac: Every allocate, vacate and transfer writes an immutable log row
The log captures actor, action, timestamps, previous and new state
Log rows cannot be edited or deleted through the application
History is visible on the resident profile and the room page
out: No export of the audit trail in the MVP.
